venue: U.S. Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Privacy, Technology, and the Law
title: Oversight of A.I.: Rules for Artificial Intelligence (S. Hrg. 118-37)
where: official transcript has no timestamps; items cited by questioner

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Kennedy
decisions.quote: I would form a new agency that licenses any effort above a certain scale of capabilities and can take that license away and ensure compliance with safety standards.

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Graham on suing AI companies
decisions.quote: I think there needs to be clear responsibility by the companies.
decisions.note: Set against OpenAI backing the 2026 Illinois liability shield.

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Booker on ads
decisions.quote: I wouldn't say never. Like, I think there may be people that we want to offer services to, and there's no other model that works, but I really like having a subscription-based model.
decisions.note: He did not rule ads out in 2023. Fairness context for the ads entries.
decisions.record: added to the note of openai/2024-05-harvard-ads-last-resort

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Ossoff on kids
decisions.quote: I think we try to design systems that do not maximize for engagement. In fact, we're so short on GPUs, the less people use our products, the better. But we're not an advertising-based model.
decisions.note: Context for the ads and engagement entries; not separately checkable.

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Hirono on harmful requests
decisions.quote: Not that we think adult content is inherently harmful, but there's things that could be associated with that that we cannot reliably enough differentiate, so we refuse all of it.
decisions.note: The 2025 erotica decision was tied to age prediction, which is consistent with this reasoning.

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Graham on drones
decisions.quote: I think we shouldn't allow that.
decisions.note: On a drone selecting its own target. OpenAI's 2026 Pentagon contract language claims a human-responsibility limit on autonomous weapons; already covered by the Pentagon entries.

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Hawley on the pause letter
decisions.quote: We are not currently training what will be GPT-5. We don't have plans to do it in the next 6 months.
decisions.note: Consistent with OpenAI's May 2024 statement that it had recently begun training its next frontier model. Kept, not entry-worthy.

decisions.at: answer to Chair Blumenthal on privacy
decisions.quote: One is that we don't train on any data submitted to our API.
decisions.note: The API data policy in force then; graded in the commitment inventory (W2).

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Kennedy on pay
decisions.quote: I have no equity in OpenAI.
decisions.note: True when said; no claim to check.

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Kennedy
decisions.quote: We will do that.
decisions.note: Promise to send a list of dangerous-capability tests to Sen. Kennedy's office. Not checkable from outside; logged, no entry.

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Hirono
decisions.quote: I think it'd be a great policy to say generated images need to be made clear in all contexts that they were generated.
decisions.note: OpenAI added C2PA metadata to DALL-E 3 images in February 2024.

venue: U.S. Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Privacy, Technology, and the Law
title: Oversight of A.I.: Principles for Regulation
where: official transcript has no timestamps; items cited by questioner

decisions.at: written statement
decisions.quote: a straightforward extrapolation of today's systems to those we expect to see in 2 to 3 years suggests a substantial risk that AI systems will be able to fill in all the missing pieces, enabling many more actors to carry out large-scale biological attacks
decisions.note: A dated prediction (mid-2025 to mid-2026). Anthropic switched on ASL-3 protections in May 2025, inside the window; no public evidence of AI-enabled large-scale biological attacks. The capability half was, on Anthropic's own assessment, roughly borne out.

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Blumenthal on timing
decisions.quote: I would really target 2025, 2026, maybe even some chance of 2024.
decisions.note: Part of the same prediction; used in that entry.

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Hawley on Google
decisions.quote: They don't control any board seats, but yes, Google is an investor in Anthropic.
decisions.note: True when said.

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Hawley on privacy
decisions.quote: We don't train on, you know, publicly available information.
decisions.note: Almost certainly a slip: Anthropic's model cards say training data includes public web data. Not a claim to hold Anthropic to; no entry.

decisions.at: answer on data-labelling labor
decisions.quote: northwards of 75 percent workers from the U.S. and Canada and all paid above the California minimum wage
decisions.note: Hedged ("I believe"); not checkable from outside.

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Blumenthal on recalls
decisions.quote: I think such requirements make sense.
decisions.note: On incident reporting and recall powers; context for the SB 1047 entry.

decisions.at: answer on open source
decisions.note: Views on open-weight release; no claim to check.

venue: U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation
title: Winning the AI Race: Strengthening U.S. Capabilities in Computing and Innovation (S. Hrg. 119-143)
read: full, including the prepared statement and Altman's written answers to questions for the record
where: official transcript has no timestamps; items cited by questioner

decisions.at: answer to Chairman Cruz on prior approval
decisions.quote: I think that would be disastrous.
decisions.record: already an entry (openai/2025-05-08-altman-senate-disastrous); added the official transcript, the quote, and his answer to Sen. Schatz for balance

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Schatz
decisions.quote: No. I think some policy is good.
decisions.note: Asked if self-regulation is enough. Added to the disastrous entry's note for balance.

decisions.at: prepared statement
decisions.quote: That's why we red-team relentlessly and lead the industry in transparency.
decisions.note: Three weeks after GPT-4.1 shipped without a system card.

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Blunt Rochester on the restructuring
decisions.quote: We never planned to have the nonprofit convert into anything.
decisions.note: The dispute had been about control, which the May 5 reversal kept with the nonprofit.

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Moreno on children
decisions.quote: One thing we say a lot internally is we want to treat our adult users like adults.
decisions.note: The October 2025 erotica principle, five months earlier.

decisions.at: prepared statement
decisions.quote: we are now confident that we'll reach that milestone during President Trump's time in office
decisions.note: AGI by January 2029. A dated prediction with no agreed test; logged, no entry.

decisions.at: prepared statement
decisions.quote: In 2025, we will release AI-powered tools that can handle sophisticated software engineering, and AI agents that can handle real- world tasks like making doctor's appointments
decisions.note: Codex (May 2025) and ChatGPT agent (July 2025) shipped. Kept; not entry-worthy on its own.

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Budd
decisions.quote: we are going to release an open source model that we believe will be the leading model this summer
decisions.note: gpt-oss shipped August 5, 2025; already tracked in openai/2025-03-31-open-weights-no-catastrophic-risk (kept).

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Klobuchar on hallucinations
decisions.quote: On the whole, AI hallucinations are getting much better.
decisions.note: OpenAI's own April 2025 o3 system card showed higher hallucination rates than o1 on its PersonQA test, but the multi-year trend claim is defensible. No entry.

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Duckworth
decisions.quote: It is the only partnership where we have given a copy of our model weights to another organization.
decisions.note: Microsoft runs OpenAI models on Azure under its license; probably meant an outside deployment. Not checkable as stated; no entry.

decisions.at: written answer to Sen. Schatz, Q12
decisions.quote: OpenAI continues to prioritize the safe, secure, and transparent development and use of AI technology.
decisions.note: Answer to whether OpenAI still keeps the 2023 White House commitments; it does not say yes. Evidence for the commitment inventory (W2).

decisions.at: written answer to Sen. Schatz, Q13
decisions.quote: OpenAI remains committed to fulfilling the voluntary Frontier AI Safety Commitments made at the Seoul AI Summit in May 2024.
decisions.note: Evidence for W2.

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Lummis
decisions.note: Supports one light-touch federal framework over state laws; context for the preemption entries.

decisions.at: answer to Sen. Moran
decisions.note: Flags AI privacy as "one of the most important issues"; no checkable claim.
